prose:
The holidays are one of the most popular times of year to propose: the city is lit up, everyone is in a good mood, and family is often close by to celebrate afterwards. Vancouver makes it easy, with light festivals, snowy mountain tops and quiet beaches all within a short drive.

Here are my favourite places to propose in and around Vancouver this holiday season, with 2026 dates, plus how to plan it so the moment is captured properly.

1. VanDusen Festival of Lights

More than a million lights across about 15 acres of VanDusen Botanical Garden. Quiet corners of the garden make it easy to find a moment away from the crowds.

  • Dates: November 27, 2026 to January 3, 2027 (closed December 25).
  • Hours: 4 pm to 10 pm, last entry 9 pm. Timed tickets, so book ahead.
  • Tip: weeknights early in the season are the calmest.

2. Canyon Lights at Capilano Suspension Bridge Park

The suspension bridge, treetops and cliffside walkway glow with millions of lights in Canyon Lights' 20th year. Proposing on the bridge itself is a classic, and the Cliffwalk is a beautiful backup.

  • Dates: November 20, 2026 to January 10, 2027 (closed December 25).
  • Hours: 11 am to 10 pm, last entry 9 pm.
  • Tip: arrive just before dark to see it in both light and lights.

3. Peak of Christmas on Grouse Mountain

Snow, an outdoor skating pond and a lit-up Light Walk around Blue Grouse Lake, with the city twinkling below. Few places feel more like a winter fairytale.

  • Dates: November 20 to December 24, 2026, included with mountain admission.
  • Tip: mountain weather changes quickly, so check conditions on the day and dress warmly.

4. Vancouver Christmas Market at Jack Poole Plaza

A German-style market on the waterfront by Canada Place, with the North Shore mountains across the harbour. Busy and festive, so it suits a confident proposer or a ring reveal after a walk along the water.

  • Dates: November 16 to December 24, 2026. Ticketed entry.

5. Free and Quiet Spots

  • Lights at Lafarge, Coquitlam: free lights around Lafarge Lake, opening November 27.
  • Stanley Park Seawall at sunset: no tickets, no crowds on a winter weekday, and a soft glow over English Bay.
  • Bowen Lookout in winter: the winter trail on Cypress Mountain leads to a huge view over Howe Sound. It's where Jake proposed to Hannah (photos below). Read the Bowen Lookout proposal guide for winter access.

How to Plan a Holiday Proposal

  • Book early. Weekends in December and the days around Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve fill first, for venues and for photographers.
  • Plan around the light. December evenings get dark early. A proposal at sunset, or right beside the brightest displays, gives the best photos. I'll check sunset and the light at your exact spot.
  • Check the venue's rules. Some ticketed venues have rules for professional photographers. I'll confirm with them before your date.
  • Have a weather backup. Rain is part of a Vancouver winter. A covered spot nearby keeps the plan intact.
  • Keep the cover story simple. "Let's go see the lights" raises no suspicion at all.
